title: Energy stored in a wooden wheelhead at the speeds potters use
description: Bar chart of the kinetic energy held by a replica Greek wheelhead 0.81 m across and weighing 27.8 kg, treated as a uniform disc, at four speeds. At 50 revolutions a minute, about the slowest smoothing speed measured on it, 31 joules. At 75, a typical throwing speed, 70 joules. At 100, the speed suggested for Uruk wheel-coiling, 125 joules. At 120, the most measured on Egyptian turntable replicas, 180 joules. The energy is this frame's arithmetic, one half I omega squared.
heading: ENERGY IN THE SPINNING WHEELHEAD · JOULES
